original.target_description: Study 1; young adult monolinguals/bilinguals; median correct reaction times; block type by language status interaction in global-switch-cost ANOVA.

n.location: Participants, article p. 2 (PDF p. 3); Results, article p. 4 (PDF p. 5)
n.quote: Sixty-eight young adults (44 female; M = 19.1 years old; 37 monolinguals) participated [...] Two participants (both monolingual) were removed because of error rates in a cell greater than 25%.
n.sample_role: Participants in median reaction-time ANOVA: 35 monolinguals and 31 bilinguals; analytic total established as 68 recruited minus 2 excluded, corroborated by F(1,64).
n.exclusions: Two monolingual participants excluded for cell error rates >25%; only correct-response trials preceded by a correct-response trial included.

es.location: Results, printed article p. 4 (PDF p. 5 including cover)
es.quote: an interaction between block type and language status, F(1,64) = 4.9, p = .03, η2 p = .07

p.location: Results, printed article p. 4 (PDF p. 5 including cover)
p.quote: an interaction between block type and language status, F(1,64) = 4.9, p = .03, η2 p = .07

replication.target_description: Study 1; final young adult monolingual/bilingual sample; correct reaction times; block type by language status interaction in global-switch-cost ANOVA.

n.quote: this resulted in a final sample of 78 participants. This sample comprised 31 bilinguals (80.65% female) and 47 monolinguals (66% female).
n.sample_role: Final analytic participants in reaction-time ANOVA: 31 bilinguals and 47 monolinguals; F denominator df 76 corroborates full final sample.
n.exclusions: Initial 92: 3 excluded for elementary English, 3 for pure-block accuracy below 70%, 8 outliers (±3 SD on pure or switch blocks). Only correct-response trials included; data points ±3 SD removed.

es.quote: A significant interaction was found between block type and language status [F(1, 76) = 4.063, p =.047, η 2 p =.051]

p.quote: A significant interaction was found between block type and language status [F(1, 76) = 4.063, p =.047, η 2 p =.051]

reported_success.quote: findings reveal a consistent GSC advantage for the bilingual participants, successfully replicating the findings reported by Wiseheart et al.

notes: Original supplied page locator counts the PDF cover; actual article pages are 4 for GSC and 5 for LSC. Original analytic n is established from explicitly reported recruitment and exclusion counts, not a printed analytic-total numeral. Success verdict is the authors’ narrative for the GSC family, not a separately stated verdict for this individual ANOVA term. Printed metric preserved; no effect-size or p-value conversion.
